role_evaluation_tasks.task: ADR set (arch eval 1): given a growth-stage product brief, produce >=3 ADRs choosing between modular monolith and microservices; scoring rewards explicit quality-attribute trade-offs and penalizes resume-driven design.

Architecture-description review (arch eval 9, ground-truthed on lab 15 eShop pack): score a reverse-architecture pack (arc42 + C4 + ADRs) against the ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 description checklist; penalize 42010/C4/arc42 conformance claims stated without explicit mapping, missing stakeholder->concern->viewpoint traceability, and ATAM risks that do not trace back to scenarios.
Plan diagnosis (arch eval 2): given a Postgres EXPLAIN ANALYZE dump with row-estimate divergence, localize the statistics problem and propose the cheapest correct fix (ground-truthed against lab 5).

Raft safety audit (arch eval 3, adversarial): given a partition scenario and a Raft implementation sketch, identify which of four safety properties it violates - one is a subtle election-restriction (5.4-style) bug.

Expand/contract plan (arch eval 5): given a schema change (users.email -> user_emails table, 200M rows), write the expand/contract plan with compatibility windows, backfill strategy, and rollback; any ACCESS EXCLUSIVE step without lock_timeout discipline fails.

Stale-cache incident (arch eval 4): given a 'we added a cache and users see stale data' incident, produce the failure-mode diagnosis, a mitigation with an explicit consistency window, and the SLO impact statement.

License/lifecycle audit (arch eval 6): given a dependency list including Redis 8, Valkey 9, MongoDB 8, CockroachDB 26, produce a compliant-use matrix (as of the audit date) with citations - the Redis tri-license and Cockroach Core-retirement facts are checked specifically.

Benchmark falsification design (arch eval 7): given a vendor benchmark labeled [V], design the independent benchmark that would confirm/refute it, naming coordinated-omission and warmup pitfalls to avoid.

Pinned-source comprehension (arch eval 8): read a pinned path in a case-study repo (e.g. Postgres nbtree README, Kafka replication docs) and answer five comprehension questions whose wrong answers are the common blog myths.

evaluation_tasks.task: Design-system release package (ui/ux labs 2, 5, 7): a three-tier DTCG 2025.10 token pipeline with version bump, changelog, and contrast report, plus a dual-engine accessibility audit (axe-core + pa11y) that separates automated findings from the manual checks still owed - an automated score is never presented as WCAG conformance.

Moderated usability study package: ISO 9241-11 research plan with consent and compensation records, a 6-session evidence log, and synthesis that reports n and segment per finding, scores SUS against the 68-norm percentile (never as a percentage), and declines to estimate population prevalence from qualitative data.

Prototype-fidelity drill (ui/ux labs 1, 10): label the requested prototype with its Houde-Hill question and declared fidelity (refusing to answer a role question with a hi-fi comp), then run a 7GUIs-style CRUD implementation with full keyboard support and undo/focus restoration, reporting success/error metrics.

Dark-pattern and standards-currency review: flag an asymmetric consent/cancel flow with a taxonomy citation (Brignull / Gray et al. / FTC) and propose the symmetric variant, while keeping WCAG 2.2 A+AA as the conformance baseline and refusing to present WCAG 3.0, ARIA 1.3, or APCA drafts as requirements.

Defend a cross-product design-system and research strategy: evidence-quality guardrails (observed behavior > self-report > heuristic judgment), research-repository custody with retention dates, and the documented split triggers (dedicated researcher when research cadence exceeds ~2 studies/month sustained; dedicated design-systems seat when >2 products consume one system) rather than title inflation.
